rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges image limitations, but it overstates certainty and includes some potentially fabricated specifics (e.g., large TE cells, thinned zona, no collapse) that may not be reliably confirmed from a single still image and are somewhat inconsistent with a reported 2AA/full blastocyst.

Integrates age, BMI, FSH, uterine factor, endometrial thickness, semen parameters, first-cycle status, and lifestyle reasonably well, with appropriate emphasis on uterine factor as the main modifier of prognosis; AMH absence is noted.

Reasoning is mostly logical and structured, with conclusions broadly supported by embryo quality and patient factors. Minor issues include some imprecision around implantation vs clinical pregnancy/live birth framing and speculative discussion of hydrosalpinx without confirmation.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice guidelines: single embryo transfer, optimize uterine cavity, standard luteal support, cautious stance on routine PGT-A in a first cycle with limited embryos. Slight deduction for speculative emphasis on hydrosalpinx and some nonessential testing suggestions.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and failure contingency planning, including uterine evaluation and cycle planning. Useful and specific, though some recommendations remain somewhat generic because the exact uterine diagnosis is unspecified.
